title: [WT-05] Wrappers: launch every CLI inside the task worktree with per-worktree configs
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.1 and §5.2 (configs, agents copy, grok trust; the links are WT-06).

Objective: in worktree mode the agent CLI edits W, never the control checkout, while still reaching the daemon through the control checkout.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- cwd = W for claude, codex (exec -C W), gemini and grok (--cwd W). In ps1 that means Push-Location W for EVERY CLI, including the claude launch that today runs in the launcher's cwd.
- MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control checkout. Export MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET from the claim's workspace. The proxy path stays the one resolved from the wrapper's own location.
- Run the existing per-CLI config writers with W as the config root: W/.mcp.json (sh) or the ps1 temp --mcp-config (an interactive sh seat passes --mcp-config W/.mcp.json); W/.codex/config.toml; W/.gemini/settings.json; W/.grok/config.toml plus the grok trust grant for W.
- Copy <control>/.moe/agents/*.md into W/.claude/agents/.
- A config write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, calls report_blocked and launches no CLI.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-04 (task-c20464ff64ca49fca4371dd9b5194364).

NOT in scope: Serena root, the skills and memories links, the deps notice (WT-06); landing (WT-07 onward); shared-mode launches, which must stay byte-identical; docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses, fake CLI that records its cwd and env): in worktree mode the CLI's cwd is W, MOE_PROJECT_PATH is the control checkout, and MOE_WORKTREE_PATH / MOE_TASK_BRANCH / MOE_LAND_TARGET match the claim's workspace.

postflight case: the per-CLI config lands in W (W/.mcp.json or the ps1 temp config, W/.codex/config.toml, W/.gemini/settings.json, W/.grok/config.toml) and the control checkout's copies are not rewritten.
postflight case: W/.claude/agents/*.md equals <control>/.moe/agents/*.md; a forced config-write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and launches no CLI.
postflight: every existing shared-mode launch case passes unchanged.
Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes (grep -oE diff over moe-agent.sh vs moe-agent.ps1 is empty).
The verification command exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes via node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests first, sh harness (design docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.1, §5.2).

Before any edit:
- Run moe.get_commit_scope { taskId, phase: 'postflight' }.
- All five plan paths are also declared by later WT rows, so they are CONTESTED at landing.
- They land without a wrapper-observed editing tool only if two conditions hold: each path was clean at THIS session's pre-flight, and every peerDeclared[].peerActive is false (mem:decision-contested-idle-peer-exception).
- If either condition fails, stop and comment on the task. Never hand-land or weaken attribution.

The fixture builds on WT-04 (task-c20464ff), which is DONE before this row is claimable. Reuse:
- its worktree-claim knob in scripts/tests/postflight-fake-proxy.js (agreed name FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE, a JSON `workspace` returned by claim_next_task and get_context);
- its project setup: a git repo whose HEAD is on refs/heads/moe/control.
If WT-04 landed other names, use them. This task does not edit the fake proxy. The project also needs a .moe/agents/<name>.md, and enableAgentTeams must not be false.

Add ONE compact scenario to scripts/tests/postflight.sh, e.g. `[scenario W5]`. It loops over the four CLI types: claude, codex (--codex-exec), gemini and grok (--grok-exec), each run as a worker seat in worktree mode.
- Each fake CLI is named after its type, because the wrapper derives CLI_TYPE from the --command basename (moe-agent.sh ~417-428).
- Each fake writes `pwd -P` and MOE_PROJECT_PATH, MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET (marking unset vs empty), plus argv for codex and grok, to an absolute record file under TMP_DIR. Never write through MOE_PROJECT_PATH.
- W is the fixture's workspace path (<project>/.worktrees/<taskId>).

Assert, per CLI:
(a) The cwd equals W (compare with `cd W && pwd -P`). codex argv carries `-C <W>`; grok argv carries `--cwd <W>`.
(b) MOE_PROJECT_PATH is the control project; MOE_WORKTREE_PATH is W; MOE_TASK_BRANCH is moe/task/<taskId>; MOE_LAND_TARGET is the claim's target.
(c) W holds the same configs the pre-flight writes into the control for that CLI: W/.mcp.json for every CLI (ensure_mcp_config writes it for all types), plus W/.codex/config.toml, W/.gemini/settings.json or W/.grok/config.toml. Each names the control project as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH.
(d) The control's copies are not rewritten for the task. Each writer banner names the control path exactly once (the pre-flight) and W's path exactly once: `Wrote project MCP config:`, `Codex MCP config written to:`, `Gemini MCP config written to:`, `Grok MCP config written to:`.
(e) W/.claude/agents/*.md is the same file set as <control>/.moe/agents/*.md and byte-identical (cmp). For grok, the fake HOME's .grok/trusted_folders.toml trusts W.

Add one failure run. Use codex with W already registered (WT-04's reuse path) and W/.codex/config.toml pre-created as a DIRECTORY. Then:
- output carries MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED;
- the fake codex never ran (no record file);
- the fake proxy's RPC log shows report_blocked with that code.

Other rules:
- Edit no existing case.
- If the new runs go through run_scope_wrapper, bump scope_expected_runs (~4905-4910) to match.
- Run the new scenario once against the unchanged wrapper and keep the RED output: the cwd and config assertions must fail.

sh wrapper, part 1: config writers and the per-task worktree phase, in scripts/moe-agent.sh.

Save rule for EVERY moe-agent.sh save in steps 2-3:
- Never patch the live file in place. Running bash seats read it at stale offsets (mem:gotcha-bash-hot-reload-incremental-parse, task-f31d415d).
- Build the complete new file as a copy on the SAME filesystem, e.g. /mnt/d/moe-scratch/c4cccb84/moe-agent.sh, and run `bash -n` on it.
- Check that the live file's sha256 is unchanged since you copied it, then make ONE `mv -f` onto scripts/moe-agent.sh.

1. Wrap the writers in place, with no re-indentation, to keep the diff small.
   - ensure_mcp_config's project `.mcp.json` part becomes `write_project_mcp_json ROOT SERENA_PROJECT`, writing ROOT/.mcp.json. ensure_mcp_config calls it with "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT".
   - The top-level codex (~918-1087), gemini (~1090-1155) and grok (~1284-1443) blocks become write_codex_config, write_gemini_config and write_grok_config, each taking ROOT and SERENA_PROJECT. For each block:
     - The `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = … ]; then` line becomes the function header (plus `local` for the two arguments).
     - The body keeps its indentation. `$PROJECT/.<cli>` becomes `$root/.<cli>`, and the Serena argument comes from the parameter.
     - `exit 1` becomes `return 1`, and grok's `grant_grok_folder_trust "$PROJECT"` becomes the root.
     - The old site becomes `if [ "$CLI_TYPE" = codex ]; then write_codex_config "$PROJECT" "$SERENA_PROJECT" || exit 1; fi`. So the shared pre-flight writes the same files, prints the same banners and exits the same way as today.
   - In every writer, the value written as the moe server's MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays "$PROJECT", the control, whatever ROOT is.
2. Set CLI_ROOT="$PROJECT" at the start of every loop iteration, next to the other per-iteration resets (~6595).
3. Add `prepare_worktree_launch`. Call it directly after WT-04's provisioning succeeds (agreed: after `preflight_landing … launch`, ~7645), before the account lease and the CLI branch.
   - Not worktree mode (WT-04's per-task MOE_WORKSPACE_MODE != worktree, or no workspace from an older daemon): `export -n MOE_WORKTREE_PATH MOE_TASK_BRANCH MOE_LAND_TARGET`, then return 0. Nothing else changes, so a shared launch keeps today's env, cwd and argv.
   - Worktree mode:
     - Set CLI_ROOT="$MOE_WORKTREE_PATH" (W in this wrapper's path syntax, per WT-04) and export the three variables.
     - Write into CLI_ROOT what the pre-flight writes into the control for this CLI: write_project_mcp_json, plus the CLI's own writer. The grok writer also grants grok folder trust for W.
     - Copy <control>/.moe/agents/*.md into "$CLI_ROOT/.claude/agents/", overwriting, under the pre-flight mirror's gate (ENABLE_AGENT_TEAMS true and .moe/agents present).
   - The per-task writers run after daemon-host discovery and already read an exported MOE_DAEMON_HOST, so W's TOML needs no extra upsert. Confirm it is exported.
   - WT-06 will insert its Serena root and link step at the top of the worktree branch, before the writes. Leave no placeholder line.
4. Error handling: a failed writer or copy prints `MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED: <what> (<path>)`, takes WT-04's report_blocked plus no-launch exit path, and returns 1. It never falls back to the control's configs or a control launch.

sh wrapper, part 2: every launch site and per-launch file follows CLI_ROOT (moe-agent.sh; save per step 2's rule).

Use `${CLI_ROOT:-$PROJECT}`, never a bare $CLI_ROOT, at every changed site. scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs and moe-account-lease.test.mjs run slices of this text that define PROJECT only.

Sites to change:
- claude: the four `(apply_account_env; cd "$PROJECT" && …)` launches (~8527, 8530, 8540, 8544), and the interactive `ACCOUNT_ARGS+=(--mcp-config "$PROJECT/.mcp.json")` (~8223), for both its `-f` test and its path.

  - the argv probe (~7867), the exec pipeline (~7894-7897) and the TUI (~7910-7913), each `-C`, plus their `Command:` banners;

- gemini: both `(cd "$PROJECT" && …)` launches (~7972, 7984) and GEMINI_INSTRUCTIONS_PATH (~7936).
- grok: both launches' `cd` and `--cwd` (~8074, 8087), plus their banners.
- The account trust step (~6357): append `${MOE_WORKTREE_PATH:+"$MOE_WORKTREE_PATH"}` as moe-account-lease.mjs trust's third (launchDir) argument. Its signature is configDir projectDir [launchDir]. A shared seat's helper argv stays exactly as today, and an interactive worktree seat gets the trust key for W.

Unchanged:
- the MOE_PROJECT_PATH export (~699) and every RPC's MOE_PROJECT_PATH="$PROJECT";
- the proxy path and the heartbeat sidecar;
- the stream parser's MOE_GIT_TOP, MOE_GIT_REL and MOE_SERENA_PROJECT_ROOT. Attribution inside W is WT-07.

prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs, sh side:
- One sh slice starts at the literal `        AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_PATH="$PROJECT/.codex/agent-instructions.md"`. Re-anchor it to that line's new text. Its preamble already defines PROJECT.
- Keep the exec-block anchors byte-identical: `            "$COMMAND_BIN" "${COMMAND_ARGV[@]}" \` through `            set -e`.
- No other test change on the sh side.
- Make sure the taskless-handoff.test.mjs slice markers (`DYNAMIC_CONTEXT=""` … `# -------- Pre-flight landing: recovery`) and the `# 5. Fetch context`/`# 6. Read task channel` markers still exist verbatim.

Tests, ps1 harness: the twin of step 1 in scripts/tests/postflight.ps1. Write it before step 5, and keep its RED output against the unchanged ps1.

The fakes are `.cmd` shims named claude, codex, gemini and grok, passed as -Command.
- Follow the existing ones: grok.cmd records %CD% (~909-916), and codex is codex.cmd plus codex-impl.ps1 (~918-940).
- Each records %CD%, the four variables (MOE_PROJECT_PATH, MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH, MOE_LAND_TARGET) and argv for codex and grok.
- Reuse WT-04's ps1 worktree fixture: the same fake-proxy knob and the moe/control repo.

Assert (a)-(e) as in step 1, with the ps1 banners: `Codex MCP config written to:`, `Gemini MCP config written to:` and `Grok MCP config written to:`.
- For claude, the config check is the pre-flight temp --mcp-config file. It is written once and carries MOE_PROJECT_PATH = the control. The DoD allows the ps1 temp config, so W gets no .mcp.json on ps1.

Add the same failure run (codex, W/.codex/config.toml pre-created as a directory). Expect MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, no codex record, and report_blocked carrying the code.

Other rules:
- Edit no existing case. [scenario Y]'s shared-mode `grok must run with cwd = project` stays as is.
- Adjust the $scopeScenariosRun expectations (~4169-4173) only if the new runs go through the scope runner.

ps1 wrapper, the twin of steps 2 and 3, in scripts/moe-agent.ps1. Keep it UTF-8 with a BOM (parity-check enforces this). After saving, the ParseFile errors must be empty.

1. Wrap the inline codex (~972-1120), gemini (~1121-1231) and grok (~1232-1373) blocks in place, without re-indentation, as Write-MoeCodexConfig, Write-MoeGeminiConfig and Write-MoeGrokConfig, each with -Root and -SerenaProject. Call each at its old place with $projectPath and $serenaProject, so the pre-flight writes the same files and banners and fails the same way.
   - The MOE_PROJECT_PATH written into each config stays the control ($projectPathForToml / $projectPath.ToString()).
   - The grok writer's Grant-GrokFolderTrust (~1369) takes -Root.
   - The claude temp --mcp-config (~478-559) is not changed.
2. Set `$script:cliRoot` to $projectPath's string path at the start of every loop iteration. $projectPath is a PathInfo (~373).
3. Add `Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch`. Call it directly after WT-04's provisioning (agreed: after Invoke-MoePreflightBaseline, ~6668), before the codex/gemini instruction files (~6719).
   - Shared mode or no workspace: `Remove-Item Env:MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, Env:MOE_TASK_BRANCH, Env:MOE_LAND_TARGET -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`. Nothing else.
   - Worktree mode:
     - Set $script:cliRoot = W, and set the three $env: values from WT-04's per-task variables.
     - Run the active CLI's writer with -Root W. claude keeps the temp config.
     - Copy the agents (overwrite) under the pre-flight gate ($enableAgentTeams and .moe/agents present).
   - Error handling: wrap each step in try/catch. Under $ErrorActionPreference Stop, the writers' Write-Error throws, so a failure prints `MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED: <what> (<path>)` and takes WT-04's report_blocked plus no-launch path. It never falls back to the control.
4. Location:
   - In worktree mode, `Push-Location -LiteralPath $script:cliRoot` directly before Clear-MoeAccountLease/Get-MoeAccountLease (~6878-6880).
   - The trust step's (Get-Location).ProviderPath is then W, and claude and codex, which today run in the launcher's cwd, start in W. The lease text itself stays unchanged.
   - Pop exactly once: when the CLI branch returns (before the post-flight landing), and in the loop's finally, tracked by one flag.
5. Sites that move to $script:cliRoot:
   - codex: `-C "$projectPath"` at the probe (~7047), exec (~7068) and TUI (~7089), plus their banners;
   - gemini: `Push-Location $projectPath` (~7147, 7155);
   - grok: `Push-Location $projectPath` and `--cwd "$projectPath"` (~7271-7283), plus their banners;
   - the codex/gemini instruction files (~6723-6750);
   - Get-CodexMoeServerOverride's config path (~6967).
   Unchanged: $env:MOE_PROJECT_PATH, Invoke-MoeRpc, `Start-HeartbeatSidecar -ProjectPath $projectPath` and the stream parser.
6. prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs, ps1 side:
   - Change the indexOf anchor `& $Command @CommandArgs @codexSeatArgs @codexExecOverrides exec --json -C "$projectPath" @codexSandboxArgs "$shortPrompt"` (~349) to the new exec line.
   - Add `$cliRoot=$env:MOE_TEST_DIR` to the preambles of the two ps1 slices that now read it: `    $codexUsesFileContext = $false` … `} elseif ($cliType -eq "gemini")`, and the exec pipeline.
   - No other test change.

Verification: run ONE fresh command from the repo root in WSL. Its output is the complete_task evidence:
mkdir -p /mnt/d/moe-scratch && S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/v-c4cccb84.XXXXXX) && git archive HEAD scripts docs/roles | tar -x -C "$S" && for f in scripts/moe-agent.sh scripts/moe-agent.ps1 scripts/tests/postflight.sh scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs; do cp "$f" "$S/$f" && cmp "$f" "$S/$f" || exit 1; done && printf 'Verification snapshot: %s\n' "$S" && cd "$S" && bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh && diff <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.sh | sort -u) <(grep -oE 'MOE_(WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]*' scripts/moe-agent.ps1 | sort -u) && node --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs && "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs && env $(env | awk -F= '/^(MOE_|CLAUDE)/{printf "-u %s ", $1}') MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && WSLENV=MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 "/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell

What it covers:
- It is the description's command (postflight-safe bash, parity-check, and postflight-safe powershell for DoD 6), run on a HEAD snapshot plus exactly this task's five files.
- It adds the DoD-5 code-family diff and the launcher anchor tests, under Linux node and under Windows node, which runs the ps1 engines.

How to run it:
- The ps1 harness takes about 10-12 minutes. Run the command in the background and poll it to completion; never stop at the 600 s tool cap.
- docs/roles is archived because prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs reads it.
- On a native Windows seat, run the same pieces from Git Bash, with the harness via `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell`.
- If a ps1 failure reproduces on HEAD's own scripts, it is the launch environment (mem:gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl). Say so with both outputs; never skip the check.

Adversarial self-review of this task's own diff. Load the adversarial-self-review skill. Check each of the following, and fix anything that fails:
1. Shared-mode equivalence (epic rail 4): for a shared claim, the pre-flight writes, the banners, every launch's cwd, argv and env, and the trust-helper argv are what HEAD produces. Every existing postflight case passes with no edit to its assertions.
2. MOE_PROJECT_PATH is never W anywhere: in the env, in any config written into W, or in any RPC. grep both wrappers.
3. No W failure falls back to the control: no control-path config write, no launch in the control, and no `.moe/` path created inside W.
4. ps1: every Push-Location pairs with exactly one Pop-Location on every exit path, including exceptions and the no-launch path.
5. sh: every changed site uses `${CLI_ROOT:-$PROJECT}`. Every anchor that prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs, taskless-handoff.test.mjs and moe-account-lease.test.mjs slice on still exists verbatim; grep each one.
6. Saves: moe-agent.sh was only ever replaced by a checked same-filesystem rename, and moe-agent.ps1 keeps its BOM.
7. Size (QA rejects more than 400 net changed LOC): `git diff --numstat` over the five files must come to a net added-minus-deleted of 400 or less; aim for 350 or less. If it is over, never cut a DoD test. Comment on the task with the numbers and ask the architect for a size decision before complete_task.
8. Landing: re-run moe.get_commit_scope { taskId, phase: 'postflight' }. Each owned path must have been clean at this session's pre-flight, and every contesting peer must be idle; otherwise stop and comment.
If this step changed any byte, re-run step 6's command and submit THAT fresh output.

comments.content:
@architect-bc59d28a WT-04's planner here. Your plan builds on WT-04 (task-c20464ff, rev 1). Its contract:
- Provisioned values: sh sets MOE_WT_MODE (worktree or shared), MOE_WT_PATH (W), MOE_WT_BRANCH and MOE_WT_TARGET, only after a successful provision. ps1 sets $script:MoeWtMode, MoeWtPath, MoeWtBranch and MoeWtTarget. W is derived from the seat's own git top. It is never taken from the claim's workspace.path, which a Windows daemon spells D:\.
- Seat-stopping refusal: worktree_stop CODE DETAIL (sh) / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat -Code -Detail (ps1). It prints `[ERROR] CODE: detail`, calls report_blocked once and exits 1. Route your failed config write through it with MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED.
- Tests: the held-out suite is scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs (WT-04T, task-dd5daa4b), which both harnesses run. Add your cwd/env cases there. The fake-proxy knobs are FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE, FAKE_CTX_WORKSPACE and FAKE_CTX_COMMITS.
- DoD 5: WT-04 renames moe-agent.sh's nine MOE_LAND_* env-bridge names to MOE_PY_*, so the codes diff starts empty. Any MOE_LAND_TARGET export you add must appear in both twins, comments included.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: When the claim's workspace says worktree mode, a worker seat runs every CLI (claude, codex, gemini, grok) with cwd = W, and codex/grok are told W through -C/--cwd. W carries the per-CLI MCP configs the pre-flight writes for that CLI (sh W/.mcp.json plus the CLI's own config; ps1 the CLI's own config, with claude on the existing temp --mcp-config), all naming the control checkout as MOE_PROJECT_PATH, and a copy of <control>/.moe/agents/*.md in W/.claude/agents. The CLI env carries MOE_WORKTREE_PATH, MOE_TASK_BRANCH and MOE_LAND_TARGET; MOE_PROJECT_PATH stays the control. A failed W config write prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, calls report_blocked and launches nothing. Shared mode is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: Worktree-mode fake CLIs of all four types record cwd W, MOE_PROJECT_PATH = control, and the three worktree vars matching the claim's workspace (both harnesses).
The CLI's config exists in W, and the writer banner names the control path exactly once and W's path exactly once.
W/.claude/agents/*.md is byte-identical to <control>/.moe/agents/*.md; a forced W config-write failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, launches no CLI, and report_blocked carries the code.
Every existing shared-mode postflight case passes unchanged; the MOE_WORKTREE_/LAND_/CONTROL_/BOARD_ code families match between the wrappers.
invariants: MOE_PROJECT_PATH is never W: not in the env, any config or any RPC.
No W failure falls back to the control checkout or launches a CLI.
Shared-mode launches keep today's cwd, argv, env, banners and pre-flight writes (epic rail 4).
moe-agent.sh is replaced only by a checked same-filesystem rename; moe-agent.ps1 keeps its UTF-8 BOM.
No .moe/ path is created in W (epic rail 3).
compatibility: Without a workspace field (older daemon), the claim is shared mode.
The literal anchors in prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs change only where this task rewrites the anchored line; the taskless-handoff and account-lease slices are untouched.
parity-check required strings stay in both wrappers.
approvedScope: sh: write_project_mcp_json, write_codex_config, write_gemini_config and write_grok_config (ROOT SERENA_PROJECT), CLI_ROOT, prepare_worktree_launch, and the launch, instruction-file and trust sites.

ps1: Write-MoeCodexConfig, Write-MoeGeminiConfig and Write-MoeGrokConfig (-Root -SerenaProject), $script:cliRoot, Initialize-MoeWorktreeLaunch, the worktree Push-Location around lease plus launch, and the codex, gemini and grok sites.
New W5 scenarios in postflight.sh and postflight.ps1; anchor and preamble updates in prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs.
reuse: The existing writer bodies, grant_grok_folder_trust / Grant-GrokFolderTrust and the pre-flight agents-mirror gate.
WT-04's workspace variables, block path and FAKE_CLAIM_WORKSPACE fixture.
The fake-CLI patterns: sh scenario Z and Y; ps1 grok.cmd, and codex.cmd plus codex-impl.ps1.
sourceAssumptions: scripts/moe-agent.sh ensure_mcp_config writes $PROJECT/.mcp.json for every CLI; the codex, gemini and grok writers are inline blocks that exit 1 on failure.
scripts/moe-agent.ps1 runs claude and codex in the launcher's cwd; only gemini and grok Push-Location $projectPath.
scripts/tests/prompt-cache-launcher.test.mjs anchors on the sh AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS_PATH line, the sh exec block and the ps1 exec line with -C "$projectPath".

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. Re-running the pre-flight writers by copy-pasting them for W: rejected. It would create two definitions per CLI that drift. Each writer is wrapped as a function in place, without re-indentation; the shared pre-flight calls it with the control and the per-task phase with W.
2. cwd = control with `--add-dir W`: rejected by design §5. Edits would default to the control.
3. ps1: one Push-Location W per CLI branch: rejected in favour of one push before the account lease. That covers claude and codex, which run in the launcher's cwd today, and the lease's trust step (Get-Location), without editing the lease text that moe-account-lease.test.mjs runs.
4. Writing W/.mcp.json only for claude in sh: rejected. Today's pre-flight writes the control's .mcp.json for every CLI type, so W mirrors that exactly.
5. Re-writing the ps1 claude temp --mcp-config per task: deferred to WT-06. The DoD allows the temp config, and its content is unchanged in WT-05.
